Search terms for this lesson“how do I keep my health and HUD alive across scene switches?”Full walkthrough

Yesterday your player stayed in one scene. Today you wire the Canvas HUD onto StatManager, parent that Canvas so it survives alongside DontDestroyOnLoad(), and reload the current scene cleanly inside Die().

Break It Down~10 minFull walkthrough

Keep my health and coins alive when I leave the Overworld — and show them on screen.

First, before any code: cut that into parts small enough that you could look each one up on its own.

  1. Keep one StatManager alive across scene loadsA public static StatManager original guard in Awake() destroys duplicates when a new scene loads and calls DontDestroyOnLoad(gameObject) on the first one.Read: 2.7 (where StatManager became a singleton) and DontDestroyOnLoad in the quick reference
  2. Wire the TextMeshProUGUI labels inside StatManagerTwo [SerializeField] TextMeshProUGUI fields (coinText and healthText) updated in Start(), ChangeHealth(), and ChangeCoins() — no separate HUD script needed.Read: Unity TextMeshProUGUI.text row in the reference table below
  3. Reset stats and reload the scene in Die()Inside Die(), restore health = maxHealth, halve coins = coins / 2, refresh healthText.text, and call SceneManager.LoadScene(current.name) using GetActiveScene().Read: SceneManager section in the reference table below

In 2.7 you moved health, maxHealth, and coins onto StatManager because PlayerController resets every time a scene loads. Putting coinText and healthText on that same surviving manager — and letting Die() call SceneManager.LoadScene() — means both numbers stay glued to the screen through every transition.

Your turn

Before writing a line, look at StatManager.Awake(): what two things happen if original != null && original != this when you walk into a scene that already has a StatManager in it?

In StatManager.Die(), why does SceneManager.LoadScene(current.name) NOT reset coins back to 0 even though the scene reloads?

In the Editor ~15 min

Create the HUD once and child it under the StatManager GameObject so DontDestroyOnLoad(gameObject) carries the UI from Start (index 0) into Overworld and Platformer without duplicating it:

  1. Open your starting scene (Start (index 0) or Overworld — whichever loads first in Build Profiles). Right-click the StatManager object in the Hierarchy and create a UI Canvas child (UI → Text - TextMeshPro creates both the Canvas and the first text object automatically; accept the TMP Essentials import if prompted).
  2. Rename the two TextMeshProUGUI children to HealthText and CoinText, anchor them to the top-left corner of the Canvas, and position them clearly above gameplay.
  3. Select StatManager in the Hierarchy and drag CoinText into the Coin Text slot and HealthText into the Health Text slot in the Inspector.
  4. Open File → Build Profiles (Build Settings) and verify all three scenes — Start (index 0), Overworld, and Platformer — are listed in the Scene List.
  5. Press Play, collect a coin, walk through a scene switch, and take damage until Die() fires. Confirm that both numbers survive the scene switch and reset cleanly on death.
Why child the Canvas under StatManager? When StatManager.Awake() calls DontDestroyOnLoad(gameObject), Unity preserves the GameObject and every child attached to it. And if a later scene happens to hold its own spare copy of StatManager, the if (original != null && original != this) Destroy(gameObject); guard destroys the duplicate along with its extra Canvas so two HUDs never overlap.

Socratic: Singletons & Scene Persistence

  1. If Overworld also had a StatManager in its Hierarchy, why must Destroy(gameObject) happen inside Awake() instead of waiting for Start()?
  2. Why does Die() refresh healthText.text, while coinText.text only changes on the next pickup unless you update it inside Die() too?
  3. What happens in PlayerController.Start() if you run Platformer directly from the Editor without passing through Start (index 0) — does FindAnyObjectByType<StatManager>() find a manager if none was placed in that scene?
In the CodeFull walkthrough

The question this answers“how do I keep my health and HUD alive across scene switches?”

You are editing Assets/Scripts/StatManager.cs. Open Assets/Scripts/StatManager.cs. Your original singleton guard and DontDestroyOnLoad(gameObject) are already in Awake(). Here is the HUD and death-reload code that completes it.

Step 1Import TextMeshPro and SceneManagement, and declare the UI slots

Two using directives at the top of StatManager.cs and two serialized TextMeshProUGUI fields in the class body so Inspector UI objects can be dragged straight onto the manager.

using TMPro;
using UnityEngine.SceneManagement;

    [SerializeField] TextMeshProUGUI coinText;
    [SerializeField] TextMeshProUGUI healthText;
  1. 1Brings TextMeshProUGUI into scope so C# knows what type coinText and healthText are.
  2. 2Brings Scene and SceneManager into scope for Die().
  3. 4Inspector slot pointing at the Coins TMP text object on your Canvas.Storing text references on StatManager avoids a second script. The manager already runs whenever ChangeCoins() or ChangeHealth() is called, so updating the label right there guarantees the screen can never drift out of sync with the variable.
  4. 5Inspector slot pointing at the Health TMP text object on your Canvas.

Step 2Initialize the labels in Start() and update them when values change

Write the starting labels once in Start(), then refresh them inside ChangeHealth(int amount) and ChangeCoins(int amount) right after clamping.

    void Start()
    {
        health = maxHealth;
        coinText.text = "Coins: " +coins;
        healthText.text = "Health: " +health;
    }

        healthText.text = "Health: " +health;
  1. 1Runs once after Awake() finishes on the surviving StatManager.
  2. 3Starts the player at full health (3 by default).
  3. 4Sets the initial coin readout so it does not stay as placeholder text ("New Text").
  4. 5Sets the initial health readout on frame 1.
  5. 8Add this line at the bottom of ChangeHealth(int amount) (right before if (health <= 0)), and add coinText.text = "Coins: " +coins; inside ChangeCoins(int amount).

Step 3Reset stats and reload the current scene in Die()

When health <= 0, ChangeHealth() calls Die(). Reset health, halve coins, update the text, and reload whichever scene the player died in.

    public void Die()
    {
        health = maxHealth;
        healthText.text = "Health: " +health;
        coins = coins / 2;
        Scene current = SceneManager.GetActiveScene();
        SceneManager.LoadScene(current.name);
    }
  1. 1Called whenever health <= 0. Must be public or callable from ChangeHealth().
  2. 3Refills health to 3 so the next life does not immediately die again.
  3. 4Updates the HUD immediately after restoring health.
  4. 5Integer division penalty: lose half your coins on death.Integer division drops fractions automatically. 5 / 2 becomes 2 without any rounding call — a useful reminder when numbers are int.
  5. 6Asks Unity which scene is currently open (works for both "Overworld" and "Platformer").
  6. 7Reloads the active scene by name, respawning enemies, coins, and the player at the start point.
Check your work: the finished filebuild it as you read — then open this to check every line

Notice what is NOT in StatManager.cs: a second HudController script. Because StatManager itself owns both health/coins and healthText/coinText, parenting your Canvas under StatManager lets one DontDestroyOnLoad object carry both data and HUD across every scene.

// ------------------------------------------------------------------
//  REFERENCE FILE — Assets/Scripts/StatManager.cs
//  Written to be read, not pasted. Build it with the walkthrough
//  above, one step at a time, then open this and compare.
//  If it is sitting in your project unchanged, that is the thing
//  to go and do now — the walkthrough is still above you.
// ------------------------------------------------------------------
using UnityEngine;
using TMPro;
using UnityEngine.SceneManagement;

public class StatManager : MonoBehaviour
{
    int health;
    int maxHealth = 3;
    int coins;

    [SerializeField] TextMeshProUGUI coinText;
    [SerializeField] TextMeshProUGUI healthText;

    public static StatManager original;

    void Awake()
    {
        if (original != null && original != this)
        {
            Destroy(gameObject);
            return;
        }

        original = this;
        DontDestroyOnLoad(gameObject);
    }

    void Start()
    {
        health = maxHealth;
        coinText.text = "Coins: " +coins;
        healthText.text = "Health: " +health;
    }

    public void ChangeHealth(int amount)
    {
        health = health + amount;
        if (health > maxHealth)
        {
            health = maxHealth;
        }

        healthText.text = "Health: " +health;

        if (health <= 0)
        {
            Die();
        }
    }

    public void ChangeCoins(int amount)
    {
        coins = coins + amount;
        if (coins < 0)
        {
            coins = 0;
        }

        coinText.text = "Coins: " +coins;
    }

    public void Die()
    {
        health = maxHealth;
        healthText.text = "Health: " +health;
        coins = coins / 2;
        Scene current = SceneManager.GetActiveScene();
        SceneManager.LoadScene(current.name);
    }
}
Quick Reference: Persistence & Scene API Read
MemberWhat it doesGotcha
public static StatManager original; Shared class-level slot holding the one surviving manager instance. Check if (original != null && original != this) before calling DontDestroyOnLoad().
DontDestroyOnLoad(gameObject); Keeps this GameObject (and child Canvas HUD) alive when loading a new scene. Only works reliably on root GameObjects — do not nest StatManager under another object.
TextMeshProUGUI.text Sets the visible string on screen (e.g. "Coins: " +coins). Requires using TMPro; and assigning the Inspector field before pressing Play.
SceneManager.GetActiveScene() Returns the current Scene struct so current.name gives the scene name. Requires using UnityEngine.SceneManagement; and scenes added in Build Profiles.
SceneManager.LoadScene(current.name) Reloads the current scene from scratch on death. Scene-local pickups and enemies reset; StatManager fields do not unless you reset them in Die().
